in_text_mentions: presented with bilateral palmar paresthesia, hand pain, swelling, and pain in her distal interphalangeal (DIP), proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints, and metacarpophalangeal joint (MCP) (Figures 1, 2) as well as her right second toe. Physical examination revealed skin thickening in her palms and fingers, nodular contractures, and reduced grip strength (Figure 3). Laboratory findings indicated an elevated speckled pattern ANA titer, high ferritin, and low hemoglobin levels while imaging revealed diminished joint spaces in the hands indicative of osteoarthritic changes (Figures 4, 5).
